title: search: a member's global search answers 403 for the whole request when its scope includes any object the member cannot read — the console shows "No results found"
body:
Found in the 17.7 pre-release console run #21784 (`search.console-global-search`, outside the item's clauses) and confirmed by an independent verifier (RUNNER rule 7) on current `main`. It fails closed: no data, counts, ids or snippets cross the boundary, and the outcome does not depend on what the query matches. Severity: P2 (global search is unusable for restricted members). Predates 17.6.0.

## Reproduction

1. Boot the showcase. Invite a member and sign them up; give them a position that can read some objects but not all of them.
2. As the member, `GET /api/v1/search?q={any}` with no `objects` filter.

- Expected: hits from the objects the member can read; objects they cannot read are skipped.
- Actual: `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` for the whole request, whatever the query. Scoping `objects` to readable objects answers 200. In the console, the command palette sends a scope that includes an unreadable object, so it shows "No results found." with no error.

## Mechanism

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` `searchAll` (catch around L13939) continues past a missing table but re-throws every other error, including the object-level permission denial raised before the query runs. Its comment says object authorization is enforced at the REST door first; it is not — the search route checks authentication only.

## Done when

`searchAll` skips objects the caller cannot read (pre-filter by the security service, or treat the typed permission denial like a missing table), keeps failing closed on every other error, never names skipped objects, and a dogfood test proves a restricted member gets hits from readable objects.
